_comment: One manifest per client install. This file is the ONLY thing that differs
between installs. Everything else (worker code, schema, migrations, the MCP
server) is identical across every client, which is what makes an upgrade
possible without rebuilding by hand.
It lives in the CLIENT's repo, in the CLIENT's account. We keep a copy only
while engaged, and it contains no secrets: every credential is a reference
to a secret store, never a value.

infrastructure._comment: Client-owned. We hold a scoped, expiring token and nothing else.

_token_scopes: The API token the client issues us needs exactly these, no more:
Account > Workers R2 Storage: Edit   (only if r2_bucket is set)
Vectorize Edit was verified on 2026-08-23 for index creation and every
metadata index. `npx wrangler@4 login` is only a fallback for an older
token that does not carry that permission.
The account must ALSO be on the Workers Paid plan, 5 USD a month minimum.
Free can create Vectorize, but its vector, daily-write, and Worker CPU limits are prototype-scale. Paid is the supported production baseline.
_drain_cron_comment: Moves newly ingested chunks from D1 into Vectorize. It exists because
there is no transaction across the two, so a chunk lands in D1 first and
is embedded after. Until it drains, that chunk is findable by keyword and
invisible to semantic search, and NOTHING else reports that: both systems
are up and every health probe passes. `brain health` reads the backlog.

_comment: Migration and temporary rollback compatibility only. It is not a higher
product tier and it is not enabled automatically at any corpus size.
D1 plus Vectorize is the standard architecture every client installs.
A different backend requires a measured eval failure, a diagnosed cause
and an explicit architecture decision. Chunk count alone is not a trigger.
supabase.trigger_for_enabling: no automatic trigger; migration or temporary rollback only
supabase.comfortable_below: not defined; prove retrieval quality with the full eval set

corpora._comment: Which sources this install ingests. Each maps to a connector.

upload._comment: Manual drop zone. Always on: it is the fallback for anything with no connector.

retrieval._comment: answer_model runs through the CLIENT's own Cloudflare Workers AI binding, so no external model credential is required.

safety._comment: Non-negotiable defaults. The scanner is what makes 'we store nothing dangerous' true rather than aspirational.

_ingest_cron_comment: On macOS this installs as a per-user LaunchAgent and runs Google Drive
normally incrementally, with periodic and policy-triggered full comparisons.
The plist contains no credentials. Calendar times use
the Mac's local timezone, which the installer compares with client.timezone.
Standard brain setup fills admin_key_secret with a deterministic, non-secret
macOS Keychain locator before generating a key. An existing legacy adjacent
.brain-admin-key is preserved. Windows uses a DPAPI-protected adjacent file;
Linux uses an owner-only adjacent file. Never put the key itself here.
brain secrets updates and verifies that declared durable location.
google_token_store persists auto, keychain or file for unattended runs.

_comment: Filled from section 6 of the intake questionnaire, in the CLIENT'S OWN
WORDS. Do not tidy them into better English: 'why did we stop using
those guys' retrieves differently than 'vendor termination rationale',
and theirs is the phrasing that has to work.
These do double duty. The acceptance suite uses them as retrieval probes,
so a passing install is one that answers THIS client's questions rather
than generic ones. And they are the kickoff script: the first thing the
client sees is their own ten questions answered with citations.
_expected_to_fail_note: Two questions the client predicts it will get wrong, captured at intake.
Shown at kickoff alongside the wins. A tool that says what it does not
know is worth more than one that always sounds confident, and predicting
the misses in advance turns the gap list into honesty rather than failure.

_comment: The priority slice goes in FIRST and gets proven before the long tail
streams in behind it. Do NOT ingest chronologically: order by likely
answer value, usually the last 12 to 24 months plus every meeting
transcript. A default tuned for steady state quietly ruins the first
impression, which is the one that decides whether they trust it.

priority_slice.note: from intake question 2.4, the single folder that would already be worth it

_comment: As of v0.1 everyone with access sees everything indexed. Document-level
permissions are NOT built. Any client with employees who must not share
sight of every document is out of scope until ACLs ship. This field exists
so the limitation is explicit in the install record rather than discovered
later.

handoff._comment: On handoff, the client revokes our token and this records the date. After that we hold nothing.
